result.title: High-resolution tactile observation makes hidden racket-control mechanisms learnable
result.comment: 58 pages, including 14 pages of main text and 44 pages of supplementary information. 5 main figures and 19 supplementary figures
result.summary: Experts can master fine hand-object manipulation skills, yet limited conscious perception of rapid tactile interactions hinders their ability to articulate the underlying control mechanisms. Badminton racket control requires rapid, fine hand-force coordination, providing a demanding testbed for uncovering these mechanisms. An 864-node tactile-inertial glove with synchronized 100-Hz acquisition recorded over 14,000 strokes from more than 70 participants across five skills. Inspired by sensorimotor control, our mechanics-grounded two-layer framework inferred object-driving and grip-stabilizing control from tactile history, while resolving their spatiotemporal force realization. We found that higher proficiency was associated with selective rather than extensive control: greater skill specificity, anticipatory regulation, focal distal modulation and lower geometric torque cancellation, while spatiotemporal coordination showed a non-monotonic acquire-refine pattern. We translated these mechanisms into personalized guidance targeting force control and force-motion coordination. In a randomized cohort, mechanism-guided learners gained 0.72 expert-rated skill levels versus 0.05 with level-only feedback, making control mechanisms actionable.

AI.brief_summary: 用864节点触觉-惯性手套采集70余名参与者、14000余次羽毛球拍控球数据，提出两层力学框架从触觉历史推断物体驱动与握持稳定这两类隐藏控制；发现高水平表现对应选择性而非广域的调制、预期性调节与更集中的远端调控，并将机制转化为个性化指导，在随机队列中验证有效。
AI.relevance_reason: 从高频触觉历史反推隐藏控制变量的框架，可能与 LVR 中如何由观测历史维护任务必要的物理性 latent 状态、以及「选择性调制优于全面调制」的假设可供类比核查，但该文不涉及视觉语言推理，联系较远。
